items.title: Stevie Wonder Announces Songs in the Key of Life 50th Anniversary Tour
items.summary:
Stevie Wonder has scheduled an 18-date tour built around Songs in the Key of Life, marking the album's 50th anniversary by performing the 1976 double record in its entirety at every stop.

The run opens overseas, beginning October 13 at Utilita Arena in Birmingham, UK, and continuing through Paris, Copenhagen, Oslo, Stockholm, Hannover, Cologne, Amsterdam, Dublin, London, Manchester and Glasgow. Wonder then returns to the United States in November for shows at Madison Square Garden on November 19, United Center in Chicago on November 21 and Capital One Arena in Washington, DC, on November 23.

Two December dates follow at the Fox Theatre in Detroit, on December 8 and 9, before the tour closes December 19 at Intuit Dome in Los Angeles. The Detroit shows carry particular weight given the city's role in Wonder's career at Motown.

Consequence reported the ticketing details: general on-sale for the US dates, excluding Detroit, begins Thursday, September 10 at 10 a.m. local time through Ticketmaster, with the Detroit shows following on Tuesday, September 15 at the same hour. No public presales have been announced for the American leg.

The UK and European dates operate on a separate schedule, with a presale starting Wednesday, September 9 and general tickets going on sale Friday, September 11 at 10 a.m. local time.

Songs in the Key of Life arrived in 1976 and remains the centerpiece of Wonder's catalog. This tour is the first he has organized around a full performance of it.

items.title: Animal Collective To Play Feels In Full at NYC and LA Shows
items.summary:
Animal Collective will perform their 2005 album Feels in full at two shows this October, the band's first live appearances together since 2022. The quartet plays Knockdown Center in Queens, New York on October 22 and the Fonda Theatre in Los Angeles on October 24.

Pitchfork reported the dates, which follow a year of activity around the record. The band issued a 20th anniversary reissue of Feels last year that collected nine previously unheard B-sides and unreleased demos, and also released FeelsLive 04/05, a compilation drawn from MiniDisc recordings of shows played in 2004 and 2005.

Feels was the group's sixth album and has held up as one of their most widely admired; Pitchfork placed it at No. 55 on its list of the 200 best albums of the 2000s. The reissue and the archival live set made a full-album performance feel like the logical next step.

Animal Collective's most recent studio album, Isn't It Now?, arrived in 2023. In the time since, Panda Bear, Avey Tare and Geologist have each released solo projects, and Geologist worked with Deakin last year on the score for Jetty, a documentary about rebuilding New York's Rockaway Beach after Hurricane Sandy.

Two shows, two coasts, one album. That is the whole of the announcement for now.

items.title: ‘Star Wars: Starfighter’ & ‘Star Wars’ 50th Anniversary Edition To Be Released In Imax 70MM
items.summary:
Lucasfilm and Imax will release Star Wars: Starfighter and a 50th anniversary re-release of the original Star Wars in Imax 70mm in 2027, the first time the franchise has appeared in that format.

Deadline reported that the 1977 George Lucas film will open February 19, 2027, marking its first Imax presentation of any kind, digital or film. Starfighter arrives May 28, 2027, the 50th anniversary weekend of the original's release.

Shawn Levy directs and produces Starfighter, a standalone story starring Ryan Gosling as Kade Auberon, a cynical rogue pulled across the galaxy by his own past. The cast also includes Matt Smith, Mia Goth, Aaron Pierre, Jamael Westman, Daniel Ings, Flynn Gray and Amy Adams, from a script by Jonathan Tropper, with Kathleen Kennedy producing alongside Levy.

The film was shot with Imax-certified cameras under the Filmed For Imax program and will be converted to 70mm prints for a small set of film-equipped theaters. Imax 70mm dates to the company's founding 60 years ago and remains available in only a handful of cinemas worldwide.

Those screens have been unusually productive this year, taking in a record $78 million globally for a per-screen average of $1.9 million. Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey drove much of that, becoming Imax's highest-grossing title ever with more than $486 million, roughly 30 percent of the film's $1.63 billion worldwide total.

items.title: ‘South Park’ Changes Name to ‘South America’ as Creators Roast Apple and Google for Obeying Trump’s Lake America Name Change
items.summary:
Trey Parker and Matt Stone say they are renaming South Park. Ahead of the show's 29th season premiere, the creators announced the series will now be called South America, a joke aimed squarely at the tech companies that have complied with President Donald Trump's geographic renaming orders.

"Inspired by the bravery and patriotism of Apple and Google, we are changing the name of South Park to South America," the pair said in a statement reported by Variety. They added: "We especially want to thank our parent company Paramount, a Skydance Capitulation."

The gag responds to a run of executive renamings. Trump decreed the Gulf of Mexico would become the Gulf of America, a change Google and Apple both reflected in their mapping apps, and more recently said his administration would refer to Lake Ontario as Lake America following a trade dispute with Canada. He also shared a video on social media suggesting New Mexico could become New America.

South Park has spent its recent run on Trump directly. The show's most recent season depicted the president as Satan's lover, echoing its old treatment of Saddam Hussein, and cast Vice President JD Vance as Tattoo from Fantasy Island. That season won the Creative Arts Emmy for Outstanding Animated Program, an occasion the creators used to mock Trump again.

Season 29 premieres September 16 at 10 p.m. ET/PT on Comedy Central. New episodes stream the following day on Paramount+ in the United States, Canada and Australia.

items.title: Tom Jones Alleges ‘The Voice U.K.’ Fired Him at 86 Years Old Due to ‘Financial Difficulty With Insurance’
items.summary:
Tom Jones says ITV removed him from The Voice U.K., and that the network told him the reason was insurance. The 86-year-old singer laid out his account in a social media post after weekend rumors that he would not return for the show's next series.

"To be clear, I did not want to leave The Voice as I love the show and really appreciate the audience," Jones wrote. "ITV made this decision obviously a while ago, and I was told just recently. The reason given is because of a financial difficulty with insurance." He added that the network has since described the change publicly as a refresh, and that he was offered a reduced role making appearances rather than coaching from the start. "There's never a good time to fire an 86-year-old who's still pretty good at his job," he wrote.

A spokesperson for the show told Variety: "We have loved working with Sir Tom Jones over the past nine years on The Voice U.K. While he will no longer be a full-time coach on series 15, we continue to talk to Sir Tom and his team about his involvement in the next series."

Jones has been attached to the format almost since it began. He joined the original BBC version in 2012, sat on the panel for three years, stepped away, then returned when the show moved to ITV in 2017. The Voice U.K. is produced by Lifted Entertainment, an ITV Studios subsidiary.

He is currently on screen in the run that launched August 22 and airs Saturdays on ITV, alongside will.i.am, Tom Fletcher, Danny Jones and Kelly Rowland. Will.i.am replied to Jones' Instagram post with a string of crying emojis, Anne-Marie wrote "I love you," and Season 4 contestant Karl Loxley called him "an absolute legend and a true gentleman."

ITV has not named a replacement coach for series 15.
